newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Sept coffee exports seen 1.2 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Sept coffee exports seen 1.2 mln bags.

text.p: Brazilian coffee exports in September will probably reach 1.2 million 60-kg bags, slightly below expectations, after a delay in finalising the scrapping of a state export tax, said the head of the exporters' federation.
But export in October should be the highest for any month so far this year due to shipments which had been due to take place in September, FEBEC president Oswaldo Aranha said.
"Shipments in September will be probably a little slower than we expected due to the ICMS delay," Aranha said.
"But October shipments should be well above 1.5 million bags as the month will be somewhat inflated by shipments which were not made in September for technical reasons," he added.
In August it became apparent that the government would approve a bill cutting a 13 percent state export tax on primary commodities and semi-manufactured goods.
However the necessary documentation was only completed in the middle of September after a period in which exporters held back sales in expectation of its approval.

According to today's bulletin from the Rio de Janeiro Coffee Business Center, September shipments based on bills of lading so far were 1.08 million bags and 1.32 million based on certificates of origin.
But October shipments were already running ahead of this stage last month, totalling 115,075 bags based on bills of lading against 94,070 bags by the same period in September.
Based on certificates of origin which show the intention to ship, October shipments were 436,009 bags, well up from last month's 246,396 bags at this stage.
So far the highest monthly coffee exports this year were seen in August when 1.54 million bags were sold overseas.
Under a plan agreed by members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), Brazil can ship nine million bags in the second six months of this year.
"I believe we will be very close to nine million bags, " Aranha said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
